1: On the edge of the promised land, Moses begins his farewell speeches. He recalls leaving Sinai, the spies, and the people's refusal to enter.
Remembering past failure is meant to prevent repeating it.
2: Moses recalls the long wandering and how God told Israel to pass peacefully by Edom, Moab and Ammon, then gave victory over King Sihon.
"These forty years the Lord your God has been with you; you have lacked nothing."
3: Israel defeats Og of Bashan, and the land east of the Jordan is shared out. Moses begs to enter the land, but God lets him only see it.
Moses accepts God's no and prepares Joshua to finish the work.
4: Moses urges Israel to keep the law without adding or taking away, and never to make an idol. No other nation has a god so near.
Israel's wisdom is its closeness to God.
5: Moses repeats the commandments given at Sinai to the new generation.
Each generation must receive the covenant for itself.
6: "The Lord our God is one Lord. You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul and strength." Teach these words to your children and keep them always before you.
Jesus calls this the greatest commandment. Faith is handed on at home.
7: Israel must not adopt the gods of Canaan. God chose them not because they were numerous but because he loved them.
8: God let Israel hunger and fed them with manna to teach that man does not live by bread alone. When they are prosperous they must not say, "My own power got me this."
Jesus quotes this chapter against the devil. Comfort is a greater test than hardship.
9: Israel is not given the land for its own righteousness. Moses recalls the golden calf and his forty days of pleading.
Grace is not earned. Moses stands in the gap for a stubborn people.
10: New tablets are made. What does the Lord require? To fear him, walk in his ways, love and serve him with all your heart, and love the stranger.
God looks for love from the heart, not only outward observance.
11: Love God and keep his commands, and the land will have rain and harvest. Moses sets before the people a blessing and a curse.
12: Israel must destroy the pagan shrines and offer sacrifice only at the place God will choose.
Worship is given by God, not designed to suit ourselves.
13: If a prophet, a relative or a whole town urges the worship of other gods, Israel must not listen, even if signs come true.
A miracle does not prove a message. Loyalty to God comes first.
14: Clean and unclean animals are listed again. Every third year the tithe goes to the Levite, the foreigner, the orphan and the widow.
Generosity to the poor is built into the law.
15: Every seventh year debts are released and Hebrew servants freed. "Open your hand wide to your brother, to the poor."
God wants no permanent underclass among his people.
16: Keep Passover, Weeks and Tabernacles at the sanctuary. Appoint judges who take no bribes.
"Justice, and only justice, you shall follow."
17: Hard cases go to the priests and the judge. A future king must not pile up horses, wives or gold, and must read God's law all his life.
The ruler is under God's law, not above it.
18: Israel must not practise divination or consult the dead. God will raise up a prophet like Moses and put his words in his mouth.
The New Testament sees this promise fulfilled in Jesus.
19: Cities of refuge protect those who kill by accident. No one may be convicted on the word of a single witness.
20: Before battle the priest encourages the army, and those who are newly married or afraid are sent home. Peace must be offered first.
Even war is placed under moral limits.
21: Rules for an unsolved murder, captive women, the rights of the firstborn, and a rebellious son. A hanged man's body must be buried the same day.
Paul applies the last law to Christ, who bore the curse for us on the cross.
22: Return lost property, help a fallen animal, build a rail around your roof. Laws protect marriage and punish sexual violence.
Love of neighbour is spelled out in practical detail.
23: Who may enter the assembly, cleanliness in camp, shelter for escaped slaves, no interest on loans to a brother, keeping vows.
Holiness touches every corner of life.
24: Rules on divorce, pledges and wages. Pay the labourer before sunset, and leave the gleanings for the foreigner, the orphan and the widow.
Jesus says the divorce rule was allowed because of hard hearts. God defends workers and the poor.
25: Punishment must be limited. A brother should raise children for a dead brother's name. Use honest weights and measures.
Honesty in business is a religious duty.
26: The Israelite brings the first of his harvest and recites the story: "A wandering Aramean was my father... the Lord brought us out of Egypt."
Giving thanks means remembering what God has done.
27: After crossing the Jordan the people are to write the law on stones. The Levites pronounce twelve curses on secret sins, and the people answer "Amen".
The people publicly accept responsibility for the covenant.
28: Obedience will bring blessing in city and field. Disobedience will bring disease, defeat, siege and exile, described at length.
The later history of Israel, including the exile, is read in the light of this chapter.
29: Moses gathers everyone, from leaders to water carriers, and renews the covenant, warning of what will happen if they turn away.
The covenant includes those "not here today": future generations.
30: If Israel is scattered and returns to God, he will gather them. The command is not too hard or far off. "I set before you life and death; choose life."
God respects our freedom and urges us to choose well.
31: Moses, aged 120, hands leadership to Joshua: "Be strong and courageous." The law is to be read aloud to all the people every seven years.
God's work goes on after any one leader.
32: Moses sings of God the Rock, faithful and just, and of a people who grew fat and forgot him. God will judge and then have compassion.
The song is a witness for the future: God stays faithful when his people do not.
33: Before dying, Moses gives a blessing to each tribe. "The eternal God is your dwelling place, and underneath are the everlasting arms."
He ends with blessing, not reproach.
34: Moses climbs Mount Nebo, and God shows him the whole land. He dies there, and Israel mourns thirty days. No prophet like him has arisen since.
Moses sees the promise from afar. Joshua, whose name is the same as "Jesus", leads the people in.
